learning: Iteration 5 showed that inertia controls slalom line loss (0.85 at lower inertia, 0.10 at iteration-1 inertia), and max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.064 m across all geometries tried. This race tests whether turn authority alone can bring max_error under 0.06 m. If it cannot, the limit is more likely gain balance than geometry.
notes: Tests the Builder's wheel_track 0.10 change with the controller held at the iteration-5 values, so the only change is the track. The effective turn gain rises by about 20 percent, which is the mechanism under test. Inertia is kept at the iteration-1 values because iteration 4 showed that lower inertia drives slalom line loss.
rationale: Iteration 5 (the iteration-1 geometry with the iteration-4 controller, 111.80) left max_error at 0.0616 to 0.0636 m on all tracks, still above the 0.06 m off-track limit. Slalom line loss was 0.10, so line retention is controllable at this inertia (mass 0.8, body_length 0.18). Iteration 4 showed that lower inertia (mass 0.7, body_length 0.14) pushed slalom line loss to 0.85, so inertia stays at the iteration-1 values. The Builder's geometry for this race changes only wheel_track, from 0.12 to 0.10 m. Turn rate per unit of wheel differential scales with 1/wheel_track, so this raises turn authority by about 20 percent at the same controller output. I keep the controller identical to iteration 5 (kp 3.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.2, weights -2 to +2, last_direction). That isolates the track change, and the effective loop gain rises by about 20 percent, which I expect to show up as lower max_error and possibly slightly higher steering_oscillation. I am not adjusting kp to compensate, because iteration 2 (kp 4) showed that higher gain raised line loss, and I want this race to test the Builder's track hypothesis cleanly. Expected result, not yet measured: max_error nearer 0.06 m on more trials, with slalom line loss staying near 0.1 or below. If line loss rises, the higher turn authority is the cause and I will reduce kp.
